title: Spectra-FFT | The Next Layer of Super Intelligence
excerpt: A breakthrough frequency-domain optimizer that cuts LLM training memory by over 50%. Train massive models on constrained hardware.
content_html:
AboutFeaturesFAQContact
Get Started

Train powerful AI models on half the GPU memory. Run bigger AI on the hardware you already own, and stop paying for chips you don’t need.

Get Started View Architecture

NVIDIA A100PyTorchCUDAcuFFT

In plain English

Same AI. Half the memory. Lower bills.

Training an AI model needs a lot of GPU memory, and that memory is the most expensive part of the hardware. Much of it is spent on bookkeeping rather than on the model itself. Spectra-FFT is a drop-in replacement that does the same bookkeeping in far less space.

01

The problem

AI training keeps running out of GPU memory. Teams either rent bigger, pricier machines or give up on the model they wanted to build.

02

What we did

We found a smarter way to store the training "bookkeeping" so it takes roughly half the memory, while the model learns the same way.

03

What it means for you

Train larger models on the GPUs you already have, or run the same job on smaller, cheaper cloud machines. Switching takes one line of code.

The problem · technical detail

AdamW has a memory tax. We removed it.

AdamW keeps two 32-bit states for every parameter: 8 bytes each, on top of the weights. That state is what pushes full-parameter fine-tuning into out-of-memory crashes on constrained hardware. Spectra-FFT is a new optimizer that stores far less of it.

01

Look at training differently

Gradients carry signal and noise. Spectra works in the frequency domain, where the two separate cleanly.

02

Keep only what matters

Optimizer state is stored for the part of the signal that drives learning, not for every parameter.

03

Train every weight

Full-parameter training with no low-rank adapters and a much smaller memory footprint.

Architecture

One optimizer. Same training loop. Less memory.

Spectra-FFT sits exactly where your optimizer does today. Nothing upstream or downstream changes: same model, same data, same loss, same scheduler.

01Model + dataUnchanged. Any PyTorch model, full-parameter training.

→

02Backward passStandard autograd produces gradients as usual.

→

03Spectra-FFTProprietary spectral engine. Replaces the optimizer step and its large state.

→

04Updated weightsSame format and precision. Checkpoints stay compatible.

A

Drop-in integration

One line replaces AdamW(...) with Spectra(...). Works with your existing training scripts, mixed precision and checkpointing.

B

Spectral state

Instead of two full-size states per parameter, Spectra maintains a compact representation of the training signal, which is where the 50%+ optimizer-memory reduction comes from.

C

GPU-native

Runs entirely on-device on CUDA using standard NVIDIA libraries. No CPU offloading, no custom hardware, no extra data movement.

D

Full-parameter training

Every weight is trained. This is not LoRA or an adapter, so there is no low-rank ceiling on what the model can learn.

Public

The concept, the measured results, the paper and the training logs. Everything needed to evaluate whether Spectra works.

Protected

The implementation, parameters and tuning that make it work. Available to evaluation partners under NDA.

VRAM engine

See what your model really costs to train.

AdamW baseline

Spectra-FFT

Optimizer state (estimated)—

Weights + state—

Estimate assumes bf16/fp16 weights (2 bytes/param) and fp32 AdamW momentum + variance (8 bytes/param). Spectra figure applies the ~55% optimizer-state reduction reported in our paper. Activations, gradients and KV cache are excluded and depend on batch size and sequence length.

Evidence

Read the paper. Watch the run.

Full-parameter fine-tuning inside a strict 5GB VRAM partition of an NVIDIA A100, logged end to end.

Evaluation access

Request a live Colab test.

We share a private Google Colab notebook that trains the same model twice on a standard GPU: once with AdamW, which runs out of memory, and once with Spectra-FFT, which completes. Access is granted to engineers and teams evaluating Spectra.

# What the notebook demonstrates
opt = AdamW(model.parameters())    # -> CUDA out of memory
opt = Spectra(model.parameters())  # -> trains within budget

Requests are reviewed manually, usually within 48 hours. Evaluation access is provided under a short NDA.

FAQ

Questions engineers ask first.

Q1

Does it replace AdamW?

Yes. It is a drop-in optimizer for full-parameter training, aimed at memory-constrained GPUs.

Q2

Is it open source?

Not currently. The paper describes the method and the demo lets you verify the behavior. Evaluation and partnership access is available on request.

Q3

Does convergence suffer?

Our logged runs track baseline convergence on the evaluated setup. See the paper and W&B logs for the exact configuration and limits.

Q4

Who is it for?

Teams fine-tuning models on-premise or on consumer and mid-range GPUs, where optimizer state is the bottleneck.
